category: machine translation API, hosted, paid API key only

free_tier.stated: none: the hosted API at libretranslate.com needs a paid API key (Pro USD 29 a month, Business USD 58 a month); the vendor offers no free trial and no free low-volume key
free_tier.notes: the keyless GET /frontend/settings of the hosted service reports keyRequired true, so the hosted translate endpoint refuses callers without a key. A 7 day money-back guarantee exists on the paid plans

per_object_cap.stated: 2,000 characters per request (the hosted service's charLimit setting)

retention.stated: not applicable: a translation endpoint stores nothing for the caller

tooling: REST API: POST https://libretranslate.com/translate with q, source, target and api_key. Hosted offer first: the paid Pro and Business keys; self-hosted option last: the user installs and runs the open-source server (pip install libretranslate) on a rented or free machine, which is not what this record prices
chaining: none: no free allowance to chain; the self-hosted option is the free route and ranks after every hosted offer

limits.value: bursts of up to 80 translations / minute on Pro; 200 translations / minute on Business; translations are unlimited

identity_cost.detail: the keys are bought through Stripe checkout links on the portal page; the checkout page was not opened, so that the payment method is a card is inferred from the Stripe checkout and unverified

reliability_note: a single hosted operator; the vendor states that a free low-volume key was tried in the past and stopped as not sustainable
confidence_note: the price, the absence of a free tier or trial and the request rates are quoted from the vendor's portal; the 2,000 character limit and the key requirement are read from the service's own settings endpoint; the payment method of the checkout is unverified.

evidence.proved: the Pro plan, the only entry tier, costs USD 29 a month
the vendor offers no free trial
evidence.quote: No, but we have a 7 days money-back guarantee.

evidence.proved: the vendor declines to give free low-volume keys
evidence.quote: While we would love to offer low volume keys free of charge, it's just not sustainable for us (we tried in the past).

evidence.proved: Pro allows bursts of 80 translations a minute
evidence.quote: Bursts of up to 80 translations / minute

evidence.proved: Business allows bursts of 200 translations a minute
evidence.quote: Bursts of up to 200 translations / minute

evidence.proved: the purchase is a Stripe checkout link
the hosted service reports that a key is required
the hosted service sets a 2,000 character limit
the managed hosting route is an API key from the portal, passed as api_key
evidence.quote: curl -X POST https://libretranslate.com/translate -d q="Hello" -d source=en -d target=es -d api_key=xxxxx

evidence.proved: the keyless languages list includes Chinese in simplified script as the code zh-Hans

binding_note: no free allowance exists to bind; the paid key is the gate, and the 2,000 character request size is the only per-call cap
notes: Supported languages: GET /languages answers without a key and lists language codes from en to vi, among them sq, ar, zh-Hans, zh-Hant, pt-BR, ru and uk (the list is longer than the language names that the home page menu shows). Character limit per request: 2,000. Keyless: no; the web page loads without a key but the translate API reports keyRequired true.
